build._arch_define_note: NOT a mistake / NOT board-specific. platform.txt's recipe.c.o.pattern hardcodes -DARDUINO_ARCH_NRF54L15CLEAN literally, for every board -- confirmed by reading the real recipe text, not assumed. This matches that exactly so PlatformIO-built binaries stay identical to Arduino-IDE-built ones; don't 'fix' this to say LM20 something.
build._nordic_sdc_arch_note: DIFFERENT from the L15 board's 'nrf54l' -- confirmed via boards.txt's build.nordic_sdc_arch=nrf54lm. Points at a different SoftDevice Controller lib subfolder; builder/frameworks/arduino.py must read this per-board, not hardcode it (it previously did, which would have silently linked the wrong chip's SDC libs for this board).
build._ldscript_note: Only one linker script exists for this board -- no VPR on/off variant like L15 has, because the LM20A genuinely has no VPR/NPU hardware (confirmed: Zephyr's own docs describe it as the 'NPU-less variant' of the LM20B; boards.txt's vpr_flags is a fixed =0 with no menu toggle at all, not a trimmed-away option).
build._extra_flags_note: Default menu configuration from boards.txt: BLE enabled, Zigbee/Thread/Matter disabled, 64MHz. NOTE: unlike L15, this board's base serial_flags and antenna_flags are both genuinely empty strings with no menu block offering alternatives in what was transcribed -- not an omission, that's the real default (differs from L15's default '-DNRF54L15_CLEAN_SERIAL_BRIDGE_AUTO', worth being aware this board behaves differently there until confirmed against real hardware).

upload._upload_note: pyOCD target is 'nrf54lm20a', NOT 'nrf54lm20b' -- confirmed from boards.txt's upload.target=nrf54lm20a, and independently consistent with pyOCD's actual built-in target name (added v0.44.0). Board id/core/variant all say nrf54lm20b; the chip target string specifically does not. CONFIRMED FINDING (tested against a real nRF54LM20-DK): pyOCD's nrf54lm20a target rejects that DK's chip outright ('This doesn't look like an nRF54LM20A device!') because the DK carries the nRF54LM20B SoC, not the LM20A -- two genuinely different parts, confirmed via Nordic's own DK hardware guide. pyOCD's device-ID check then still attempted an APPROTECT mass-erase unlock despite the mismatch and hit a hard memory-transfer fault mid-operation; the probe still enumerated afterward (pyocd list --probes), suggesting the DK wasn't bricked, but this was not re-attempted given no upside once the chip ID was confirmed wrong. pyOCD has NO separate nrf54lm20b target at all (confirmed via `pyocd list --targets --name nrf54lm` -- only nrf54lm20a is builtin). Build+link (not upload) WAS successfully validated against this DK's real LM20B silicon. Upload against actual XIAO nRF54LM20A hardware (where the chip and target genuinely match) is still pending -- expected Tuesday.

_memory._source: boards.txt upload.maximum_size / upload.maximum_data_size. Only one RAM figure, unlike L15's two VPR-dependent figures -- this board has no VPR state to vary.
